data.gender_notes: Balram is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bal - strong, powerful, Rama - mountain. Balram means strong as a mountain. The name Balram carries the meaning “Strong as a mountain” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Balram usually hope their child will grow to embody strong as a mountain and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Balram belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Strong as a mountain.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Balram total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Balram is an ancient name of Hindu origin, revered in Indian mythology and culture. The name is associated with strength, power, and the rugged determination of the powerful gods and heroes of Hindu mythology. Balram is also a name associated with leadership, courage, and the overcoming of obstacles.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Balram represents the inner strength and resolve that helps us overcome difficulties and challenges in life. The name is a reminder of the power within us to overcome adversity and tap into our inner resources to achieve our goals. Balram is also a symbol of devotion and faith, as the name was borne by Lord Balaram, an avatar of Lord Vishnu, who is known for his strength, courage, and loyalty to his brother and friend, Lord Krishna.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Balram is a popular Hindu name, derived from the Sanskrit words 'bal' meaning strength and 'ram' meaning God's delight or joy. It symbolizes the divine strength that comes from being in harmony with the divine and experiencing joy in the journey of life.

vedic_reference.note: Balram is a name of Lord Krishna, who was born as the eighth son of King Ajamila and Queen Devaki. He is also known as Baladeva and Balabhadra.

historical_references.reference: Balarama is a major deity in Hinduism and is considered an avatar of the god Vishnu. He is the elder brother of Krishna and is often depicted as holding a plough. Balarama is also known as Baladeva and Sankarshana.
